scope: Read-only primary-source research; only this JSON written. No CI/GitHub/app/account mutations. Existing sample CI run belongs to parent and was not accessed.

decision.emptyArrayMeaning: No verified domain set was established by this research; this is NOT a suggested NSPrivacyTrackingDomains value.
decision.noSafeDropInFix: Neither NSPrivacyTracking=false based solely on SDK delegation nor true with invented/empty domains is justified. Resolve actual endpoints and their tracking use before public submission. Removing the false key alone does not supply missing tracking domains or resolve the substantive question.
decision.correctConfigurationWhenEstablished: For actual app/SDK tracking connections, Apple prescribes NSPrivacyTracking=true and one or more correctly formatted actual tracking domains. For no tracking-domain connections Apple permits removal of both keys or false without domains. Applying either branch requires evidence of actual behavior.
decision.mixedHostConstraint: If the same hostname provides tracking with ATT and contextual delivery without ATT, declaring it may block both while ATT is denied. Apple suggests separating tracking and nontracking hostnames; for GMA this routing is controlled by Google. No app-side host fabrication, DNS rewrite, proxy workaround, or broad wildcard is proposed.
decision.priority: UNRESOLVED_RELEASE_PRIVACY_GATE; not a claim that an Apple upload necessarily fails immediately.
decision.whatWillClose: Exact SDK vendor guidance identifying applicable domains/routing, or trace plus primary-source semantic evidence identifying actual tracking connections, followed by ATT-denied regression with the proposed manifest. No observation by itself proves all future demand endpoints.

pinnedSDK.observed: GMA DeviceID collection entry sets tracking=true. The inspected GMA manifest omits top-level NSPrivacyTracking and NSPrivacyTrackingDomains; UMP has no tracking domains. Absence is an observed metadata gap, not affirmative evidence that optional IDFA traffic has no tracking destination.
pinnedSDK.notPerformed: No new device/SDK execution or archive export in this subtask.

primaryFindings.finding: Applies when an app or third-party SDK contacts domains engaged in tracking. Add true and the actual list; therefore collection being implemented only in an SDK is not itself an exemption.

primaryFindings.finding: true+empty domains is an invalid combination; false+nonempty domains is also invalid. If neither app nor SDK contacts tracking domains, remove both keys or use false without domains. plutil -lint checks plist syntax only, not complete privacy semantics.

Apple describes iOS17 blocking connections declared in any included manifest when tracking permission is absent; mixed-purpose endpoints can be separated into tracking/nontracking hosts. Points of Interest instrument flags potential tracking connections for the developer to assess. Xcode Organizer can generate an aggregate PDF.
primaryFindings.limit: The instrument's potential-tracker finding is a lead, not an automatic legal classification. No host is inferred from it without assessing its use.

primaryFindings.finding: Mobile Ads SDK Forum Advisor repeats that true requires at least one tracking domain and denied ATT can make requests to those domains fail.
primaryFindings.limit: The answer supplies NO exact AdMob hostname, no version12.14-specific recommendation, no resolution for mixed contextual/tracking traffic. It cannot authorize copying a guessed Google host.

primaryFindings.finding: SDK data-disclosure guide supports auditing data types and usage, but does not publish the required tracking-domain list for this exact configuration.

GADEnableNetworkTracing=YES enables SDK network logs. Google says support stops at13.0.0; pinned12.14 is earlier. Logs have GMA Debug BEGIN/CONTENT/FINISH framing and can span lines. No third-party certificate profile is required.
primaryFindings.limit: Confirm working output on exact12.14. This doc does not guarantee every web creative/network library request is recorded. Raw logs may contain private identifiers and encoded payloads.

primaryFindings.finding: Apple documents the Network instrument for CFNetwork HTTP activity of debuggable processes, headers/bodies and request backtraces; xctrace supports HAR export. This is an additional attribution source when GMA's log is insufficient.
primaryFindings.limit: Tool/template availability and CLI arguments must be checked on the selected Xcode; no Mac execution was performed here.

rejectedEvidence: Domains merely appearing inside ad creatives, ad-click redirect URLs or third-party ad content do not establish the SDK tracking endpoint.
Historical 2018/2021 Google forum ad request samples are too old and integration-specific to select tracking domains for GMA12.14.
Host strings embedded in an SDK binary or sample XML establish possible strings, not actual runtime use or tracking purpose.
DNS/App Privacy Report lists contacted hosts but cannot alone separate first-party scope, contextual requests, fraud prevention and cross-company tracking.
An archive privacy report aggregates declarations; it cannot discover omitted tracking domains or inspect server behavior.
An ATT enum of authorized or a nonzero ad request counter is not transport evidence.

prerequisites: Use an authorized Mac with Xcode and exact pinned dependencies. Record Xcode/iOS/device, SDK archive SHA, source commit and QA binary hash.
Use a development-signed debuggable build on a dedicated test device for physical IDFA behavior; simulator/sample runs provide narrower evidence.
Keep app/ad IDs on Google samples initially. To test Tarot's own remote routing use its unit only on a confirmed Google test device with test ad indication, no live ad clicking.
Do not enable tracing in distributed Release/TestFlight build. Owner can add the key solely to a disposable QA build Info.plist before signing; verify the final public archive lacks it.

Use private local raw logs. Do not stream xcodebuild/SDK tracing into public Actions logs or upload raw traces/HAR/xcresult/screenshots with identifiers. If CI is used, redirect private diagnostics locally and emit only reviewed redacted summaries.
Preserve authentic UMP/ATT choices. No TCF writes, fake grant, production reset or pinning bypass.
toolDiscoveryCommands: xcrun simctl spawn booted log help stream
executablePlan.QAOnlyPlistCaveat: Commands are examples for an existing disposable QA .app before code signing; if key exists inspect it rather than blindly Add. Altering an already signed app invalidates its signature; owner must integrate correctly. Do not run against production archive.
executablePlan.simulatorCaptureCommand: xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --level debug --style json --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "GMA Debug"' > "$TAROT_PRIVATE_QA_DIR/gma-network-private.jsonl"
executablePlan.simulatorCaptureCaveat: Capture starts before app launch and stops after the chosen flow. It may not expose physical IDFA behavior. Confirm console persistence/collection with the actual SDK/toolchain; absence of output is not absence of traffic.
instrumentSteps: On Mac open Instruments Network template and add Points of Interest if available; attach to the exact debug app/process on the dedicated device, before the scenario.

Alternatively use xctrace CLI after inspecting local help and actual template names. Example shape: xcrun xctrace record --template 'Network' --device "$TAROT_DEVICE_UDID" --attach "$TAROT_APP_PID" --time-limit 60s --output "$TAROT_PRIVATE_QA_DIR/allow.trace". Template/device/PID must be observed, not invented.

Inspect trace in Instruments; export table of contents with xcrun xctrace export --input "$TAROT_PRIVATE_QA_DIR/allow.trace" --toc --output "$TAROT_PRIVATE_QA_DIR/allow-toc.xml". Use an actual returned schema for later table export; no guessed XPath.
For HTTP HAR export, inspect installed xctrace export --help before using its documented --har option. Keep payload-bearing outputs private.
Correlate GMA request frames and Instruments task backtraces with consent events; do not classify a creative's own URL as an SDK request based only on its hostname.
scenarios: Required CMP unanswered: no ad-load requests; UMP endpoints are recorded separately.
EEA refusal: real reject; ATT remains unrequested when applicable; restricted eligible requests assessed.
EEA accept then ATT deny: identify actual GMA ad request hosts and identifier/consent presence without logging identifier values.
EEA accept then ATT allow on physical device: identify hosts and code-origin used for IDFA-bearing processing.
Revoke CMP after allow; revoke ATT in Settings and foreground: confirm next requests remove restricted processing.
Non-EEA and upgrade1.2 with existing UMP/first-party state: configured messages and permission behavior separately.

After an evidence-backed manifest change, repeat denied/restricted/allowed on iOS17+ to observe domain blocking and contextual-ad success/failure. Also exercise minimum iOS16 where OS manifest blocking does not provide the same safeguard.

redactedOutputSchema.endpointHost: actual host only, no query/path credentials
redactedOutputSchema.consentSignalPresent: boolean or unknown; no complete TCString
redactedOutputSchema.trackingPurposeEvidence: source linking processing to cross-company advertising/measurement

executablePlan.classificationRule: A real SDK request containing the permitted identifier plus known cross-company ad processing is strong evidence for tracking use of its host. If the same host serves eligible denied requests, mark mixed-purpose and seek Google-specific routing guidance; do not choose between inaccurate disclosure and breaking contextual ads by guesswork.

aggregatePrivacyReport.officialCLI: No supported Apple xcodebuild command for generating the Organizer PDF was established from the primary documentation reviewed. Do not invent -exportPrivacyReport or claim an equivalent official CLI exists.
aggregatePrivacyReport.verifiedOfficialPath: Use exact .xcarchive in Xcode Organizer, context menu Generate Privacy Report; save PDF privately with archive SHA. This aggregates declarations only.
aggregatePrivacyReport.CIAlternative: Read all PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy inside Products/Applications of the exact .xcarchive, validate plist syntax, record relative path/SHA/declared data and domains in a custom inventory. Label it CUSTOM_MANIFEST_INVENTORY, not the Xcode PDF or a runtime compliance certification.
aggregatePrivacyReport.inventoryPython:
import hashlib,json,pathlib,plistlib,sys
root=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
apps=root/'Products'/'Applications'
if not apps.is_dir(): raise SystemExit('Expected an xcarchive Products/Applications directory')
rows=[]
for p in sorted(apps.rglob('PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy')):
    raw=p.read_bytes(); data=plistlib.loads(raw)
    rows.append({'path':str(p.relative_to(root)),'sha256':hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),'trackingKeyPresent':'NSPrivacyTracking' in data,'tracking':data.get('NSPrivacyTracking'),'trackingDomains':data.get('NSPrivacyTrackingDomains'),'collectedData':data.get('NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes',[]),'accessedAPIs':data.get('NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes',[])})
print(json.dumps({'kind':'CUSTOM_MANIFEST_INVENTORY_NOT_XCODE_REPORT','manifests':rows,'uniqueDeclaredDomains':sorted({d for r in rows for d in (r['trackingDomains'] or [])}),'noRuntimeInference':True},indent=2))
aggregatePrivacyReport.inventoryCaveat: Python snippet is provided as an executable review aid inside this JSON only; not saved/executed as a separate script. It does not merge contradictory declarations away or infer absent=false.

vendorQuestionDraft.text: For Google Mobile Ads iOS12.14.0 without mediation, we found DeviceID tracking=true in its manifest but no top-level NSPrivacyTracking or NSPrivacyTrackingDomains. Our app uses UMP3.1 and optional ATT. Apple TN3181/3182 requires true plus actual domains when tracking connections occur. Which exact hostnames and configuration must our manifest declare for ATT-authorized IDFA use, while preserving contextual ads when ATT is denied? If tracking and contextual requests share a hostname, what supported SDK routing or manifest treatment resolves iOS17 domain blocking? Please provide version-specific guidance; we will not guess domains.
